name: consolidate_operational_entries
purpose: Merges a duplicate operational entry into a primary one: the duplicate becomes curationState consolidated and status archived (final), and the primary gains its occurrence count and a recomputed priority.
useWhen: Two entries describe the same problem and the user confirmed which one to keep.
find_operational_entry_semantic_matches returned a strong match and the user confirmed it is the same problem.
avoidWhen: The entries are only related, not the same problem: keep both (optionally note it in technicalContext via update_operational_entry).
The entry duplicates an existing activity, not another entry: use update_operational_entry with relatedTaskId + decision link_existing_task.
The entry is invalid and should be dropped: use update_operational_entry with curationState rejected + status archived + decision.

inputs.notes: Both entries must be in this project.
The entry to KEEP. Must be an active entry (not consolidated/rejected/archived).
The entry to ARCHIVE. Different from primaryEntryId.
Default: 'Consolidated into operational entry <primaryEntryId>.'

preconditions: Both entries exist in the same project.
Caller manages the project or has the project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead role.
The user confirmed the merge and which entry is primary.

errors.when: 'You do not have permission to consolidate operational duplicates'
errors.fix: Stop. Ask a project owner, product owner or delivery lead.

errors.when: 'Operational entry cannot be consolidated into itself'
errors.fix: primaryEntryId and duplicateEntryId must differ.

errors.when: 'Operational entry not found'
errors.fix: One of the ids is not in this project. Re-list with list_operational_entries.

gotchas.text: Irreversible: consolidated and archived are terminal.
NOT safe to retry: a second call adds the duplicate's occurrenceCount to the primary again.

The server does not check the states of either entry, so verify the primary is active yourself.
The duplicate's own duplicateEntryIds are cleared, so always consolidate directly into the final primary (no chains).
The semantic index is not refreshed, so the archived duplicate can still appear in find_operational_entry_semantic_matches.

You want to mark many at once: there is no bulk tool; call this once per id.
preconditions: The notification exists and belongs to the caller.
returns: Plain text (not JSON): 'Notification <id> marked as read.'

errors.when: 'Notification not found'
errors.fix: Re-list with list_notifications and use an exact id.

errors.when: 'You do not have access to this notification'
errors.fix: It belongs to another user; you can only mark your own.

gotchas.text: There is no tool to mark a notification unread again.

name: suggest_operational_entry
purpose: Asks the workspace AI to propose type, priority, impact, related activities and duplicate candidates for one entry and saves the proposal on the entry as agentSuggestion, without making any decision.
useWhen: An entry is new or under_review and a human will curate it; the suggestion speeds up classification.
You need candidate related activities and duplicate entries before classifying.
avoidWhen: You only need duplicate candidates: use find_operational_entry_semantic_matches (cheaper).
The entry already has an agentSuggestion and its text did not change: read it with get_operational_entry.
You want to record the decision: use update_operational_entry with the user's decision.
preconditions: Caller manages the project or has the project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead role (or is a platform admin).
Workspace AI is enabled with the operational entry suggestion feature and the Gemini provider configured.
The workspace AI budget is not exhausted.
returns: {suggestion: {suggestedType, suggestedPriority, confidence (0-1), impactEstimate (1-10), relatedTasks [issue ids], duplicateCandidates [entry ids], rationale}, groundingProvider, groundingSources, unavailableReason: null, model}. When AI is not configured: {suggestion: null, unavailableReason, model: null}.

errors.when: 'You do not have permission to generate operational AI suggestions'
errors.fix: The caller lacks a governance role. Triage manually or ask a project owner/product owner/delivery lead.

errors.when: suggestion: null with unavailableReason (e.g. API key not configured)
errors.fix: AI is not configured for this workspace. Continue triage manually; do not change AI configuration (owner decision).

errors.when: 'Workspace AI feature is disabled for this workspace.' / '... by global runtime policy.' / 'Workspace AI is disabled for this workspace.'
errors.fix: Feature off. Continue manually and tell the user.

errors.when: 'Workspace AI daily request limit has been reached.' / 'daily token budget' / 'monthly token budget'
errors.fix: Stop calling AI tools for this workspace and tell the user; never retry in a loop.

errors.when: 'Operational entry not found'
errors.fix: Re-list entries for the same projectId.

gotchas.text: The suggestion is advisory: never apply type/priority/decision from it without the user.
Each call is a paid Gemini call against the workspace AI budget and overwrites the previous agentSuggestion; call it once per entry, never over a whole backlog in a loop.
It writes the entry (updatedAt, audit event).
relatedTasks/duplicateCandidates are filtered to real ids but still verify them with get_issue / get_operational_entry.

name: test_webhook_subscription
purpose: Queues one 'system.test' POST to a subscription's URL so you can check that the endpoint receives it and verifies the signature.
useWhen: Right after create_webhook_subscription or after changing the URL/secret.
Diagnosing an endpoint whose deliveries are failing.
avoidWhen: You want to see delivery results: use list_webhook_deliveries.
The subscription is paused: the test will be dead-lettered; resume it first with update_webhook_subscription (if the owner agrees).
preconditions: Caller is the owner or an owner/admin member of the subscription's workspace.
API key profile includes sensitive admin tools.
The user agreed to send a test request to the external URL.
returns: Plain text (not JSON): 'Webhook subscription <id> test queued successfully.' No delivery id is returned.

errors.when: 'Webhook subscription not found'
errors.fix: Re-list with list_webhook_subscriptions(workspaceId).

errors.when: 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace'
errors.fix: Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user.

gotchas.text: Asynchronous: a background worker sends it.
Then call list_webhook_deliveries(subscriptionId) and look for eventType 'system.test': status delivered = OK; lastError (e.g. 'Webhook endpoint responded with 401') = receiver problem.
It is sent even if 'system.test' is not in the subscription's events.
Payload: {type: 'system.test', timestamp, subscriptionId, workspaceId, projectId, source: 'lpm-test'}.
Each call sends another POST.

name: update_operational_entry
purpose: Edits an operational entry's fields and moves it through the curation state machine (new -> under_review -> classified -> approved/rejected/deferred), recording human decisions.
useWhen: Triage steps: move new -> under_review, then under_review -> classified, after reading the entry.
Adding or correcting type, title, description, technicalContext, affectedArea, perceivedSeverity, impactScore, occurrenceCount or effortEstimate.
Linking the entry to an EXISTING activity: relatedTaskId + decision {decisionType: 'link_existing_task', targetTaskId}.
Recording an approve/reject/defer decision that the user explicitly made, with their rationale.
Moving an approved entry's status to in_progress or resolved as the linked work progresses.
avoidWhen: Merging duplicates: use consolidate_operational_entries (never set curationState consolidated by hand).
Creating an activity from the entry: use convert_operational_entry_to_issue (it can approve a classified entry and create the issue in one write).
Getting an AI triage proposal: use suggest_operational_entry.

inputs.notes: bug | improvement | incident | request

One step per call.

{priority, rationale, overriddenAt (ISO now), overriddenBy (your uid)} or null to remove. Governance decision.

preconditions: The entry exists in the project and the caller can read the project.
Field edits and moves to under_review/classified: any project reader.
Moves to approved, rejected or deferred: caller manages the project or has the project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead role.
approve/reject/defer and priorityOverride must be the user's or owner's explicit decision; the agent only records it.
status in_progress/resolved requires curationState approved.
returns: {id} only. Call get_operational_entry to see the resulting state, computed priority and decision.

errors.when: 'Invalid operational entry curation transition from X to Y'
errors.fix: Follow the allowed map one step per call (e.g. new -> under_review -> classified -> approved). rejected and consolidated cannot be left.

errors.when: 'Invalid operational entry status transition from X to Y'
errors.fix: Follow the status map; archived can never be reopened.

errors.when: 'Operational entry status in_progress requires approved curation' (or resolved)
errors.fix: Approve first (with the user's decision), then change status.

errors.when: 'Rejected operational entry must be archived' / 'status open is incompatible with curation state rejected'
errors.fix: Send status: 'archived' together with curationState: 'rejected'.

errors.when: 'Operational entry decision is required for this curation transition'
errors.fix: Include the decision object (decisionType, decidedBy, decidedAt, rationale).

errors.when: 'Operational entry decision decidedBy is required' / 'decidedAt is required' / 'rationale is required'
errors.fix: Fill all three: decidedBy = your uid, decidedAt = current ISO timestamp, rationale = the user's reason.

errors.when: 'Deferred operational entry requires decision revaluationDate'
errors.fix: Ask the user for a re-evaluation date and send decision.revaluationDate (ISO date).

errors.when: 'Approved operational entry with link_existing_task decision requires a linked task'
errors.fix: Send relatedTaskId (or decision.targetTaskId) with an issue id from list_issues.

errors.when: 'You do not have permission to decide operational curation'
errors.fix: Stop. Ask a project owner, product owner or delivery lead to decide.

errors.when: 'Related task not found' / 'Duplicate operational entry not found' / 'Operational entry cannot reference itself as duplicate'
errors.fix: Use ids from list_issues / list_operational_entries of the same project; never the entry's own id.

errors.when: 'Operational entry priority override requires rationale' (or overriddenBy/overriddenAt)
errors.fix: Send all four priorityOverride fields.

errors.when: 'Operational entry not found'
errors.fix: Re-list entries for the same projectId.

gotchas.text: priority and priorityScore are always recomputed (impactScore + urgency from perceivedSeverity + frequency from occurrenceCount); only priorityOverride forces a priority.
On approval without impactScore, impactScore defaults from perceivedSeverity (critical 8, high 6, medium 4, low 2).
For approved/rejected/deferred transitions the server overwrites decidedBy/decidedAt with the caller and now; in other updates they are stored as sent.
The tool description says rejected -> under_review is possible, but the code blocks it: rejected, consolidated and status archived are final everywhere.
Defer with status open (not archived) so the entry can return to under_review later.
attachments and duplicateEntryIds replace whole arrays.
Not exposed to OAuth connectors; needs an API key.

verifiedFrom: updateOperationalEntryCommand, normalizeOperationalEntryDecision, normalizeOperationalPriorityOverride, validateOperationalEntryLinks, getAllowedOperationalEntryStatusTransitions / getAllowedOperationalEntryCurationTransitions / validateOperationalEntry / OPERATIONAL_CURATION_STATE_MACHINE_HELP (src/lib/operationalEntry.ts)

name: update_webhook_subscription
purpose: Changes an existing webhook subscription's name, URL, secret, events, or pauses/reactivates it.
useWhen: The owner asks to pause (status paused) or resume (status active) a subscription.
The owner gives a new URL or rotates the shared secret.
The owner wants to change which events are sent.
avoidWhen: Moving the subscription to another workspace or project: not supported; delete_webhook_subscription then create_webhook_subscription.
Removing it for good: use delete_webhook_subscription (pausing is usually better).

inputs.notes: Empty string is ignored.
Empty string is ignored.
New shared secret from the owner. Never print it.
Replaces the whole set; at least one (same names as create_webhook_subscription).
active | paused

preconditions: Caller is the owner or an owner/admin member of the subscription's workspace.
API key profile includes sensitive admin tools.
The owner explicitly asked for the change.
returns: Updated subscription object {id, name, url, secret: null, secretPreview, events, status, updatedAt, ...}.

errors.when: 'Webhook subscription not found'
errors.fix: Re-list with list_webhook_subscriptions(workspaceId).

errors.when: 'You do not have permission to manage this workspace'
errors.fix: Only a workspace owner/admin can do this. Stop and tell the user.

errors.when: 'Select at least one webhook event'
errors.fix: events cannot be empty; to stop all events use status paused.

errors.when: 'Webhook subscription status is invalid'
errors.fix: Use active or paused.

gotchas.text: Events that happen while paused are never queued (lost, not replayed); deliveries already queued are dead-lettered with 'Subscription is not active.'.
A new secret replaces the old one immediately (no overlap): the receiver must switch at the same moment.
Fields cannot be cleared with empty strings.
